Guidance & outlook: And in that journey, I think this year we will be targeting 60 million tons, which we hope to achieve.
As CMD sahab has just mentioned, we have surpassed all the expectations and crossed the magical figure of the production which is 50 million tons.
And this year, I think the guidance would be around 1 million ton out of Deposit 4.
Growth & demand: And despite slightly sluggish prices, we've been able to achieve a PAT, an 11% growth in PAT, and all our financial indices and operating indices have been rather encouraging.
The growth of around 20% to 30% in various parameters is really a pathway which will be making it possible to achieve 100 million tons by 2030.

The 15 million ton slurry pipeline that we are building from Bacheli to Nagarnar and the pellet plant at National Mineral Development Corporation Limited June 01, 2026 Nagarnar and the grinding mill at Bacheli, this entire system would get commissioned by this month-end or maybe by around mid-July.
Margins & costs: If you see our EBITDA, it has come down from 42% to 33%, essentially because of steel business.
If we take the iron ore business standalone, our EBITDA is still at 42%.
And if we take an average EBITDA of 30 to 40%, so that would be the first year revenue.
Capex & expansion: And the capex this year has been around INR3,300 crore s, which is an all-time high capex because if you leave out the land acquisition this time, and we hope that this year we'll be able to substantially increase our capex, almost double the capex now because all our expansion plans right now are on the ground.

But I think overall the capex on acquisition, the back of the envelope calculation is wherever we stand today as of today, we should be spending INR2,000 crores to INR3,000 crore s on acquisition of assets abroad this year.
And we are right now completely, completely geared towards capacity expansion projects only, execution of capacity expansion projects.
Balance sheet & cash: Okay, so this was essentially an arrangement made for a very specific requirement of NMDC Steel where they were facing cash flows, so we stepped in and we were doing trading business with the HR coils of NMDC Steel.
That is essentially a special mechanism that as and when if there's a cash flow issue at NMDC Steel and we generally tend to step in and buy HR coil and then sell it in the market.
Sir, with respect to RINL, I mean how confident we are on the recovery of all the receivables and we've, we're paying around 1 ,500 odd crores for the land lease, 1,800 odd acres.
Risks & challenges: Of course there's a time element to that, but we don't see any risk in that.
I don't see much volatility in the very short term.
I don't think there is going to be this financial year, especially this quarter, I don't think there's to be any volatility either upside or the downside.

guidance.t: But I think overall the capex on acquisition, the back of the envelope calculation is wherever we stand today as of today, we should be spending INR2,000 crores to INR3,000 crore s on acquisition of assets abroad this year.

Guidance & outlook: And we have set ourselves a very, very steep target of 55 million tons, which is exactly 100% of our EC that we will have this year.
So we expect the NSL outstandings to be fully liquidated by the end of the year, hopefully, because already they have started some payment of around INR100 crores -- about INR200 crores a month.
Around 55.4 million tons is what we are targeting.
Growth & demand: We have a growth in PAT on an annual or a year-on-year 12-month basis of around 19% and PBT after exceptional item of around 16%, which is indeed commendable.
One is to -- the slurry pipeline that is likely to come from Kirandul, Nagarnar to Vizag, will terminate there, and we'll have to make an 8 million ton pellet plant there.
So that's a growth of more than 50%, which consequently has led a growth of our production, which was hovering around 110,000 to 120,000 to it has now gone up to 180,000, 190,000.
Margins & costs: Our production was marginally lower about -- by about 1 million ton and sales was -- did pick up at the end.
Raw material cost is almost 80% plus if I just take RM to...
In the question which was asked by Tushar earlier, as a percentage -- raw material cost as a percentage of sales, like it was 80% plus in the fourth quarter, and it was even higher earlier quarter.
Capex & expansion: We have seen that the capex was the highest this year, which was INR3,700 crores, highest ever.
And we plan to continue much higher capex so that we are able to not only execute, but also commission all the capacity building projects that we have.
Touching around 90% capacity utilization on a monthly basis is one of the fastest ramp-up for a new Greenfield plant.
Balance sheet & cash: So we are seeing a very sharp increase in receivables this year to almost INR7,800 crores.
Any debt you plan to take on their new capacity expansion or entire thing...

One more calculation, we can expect most of it would be internally financed, but whether we should -- considering our expansion plans beyond India, one call has to be taken about a year from now or about 1.5 years from now that do we leverage our balance sheet even for our domestic expansion plan.
Risks & challenges: These are -- I think our performance despite the challenges in FY '24 -- in FY '25 has been rather commendable.
And despite all these challenges, our numbers speak for themselves.
No, I don't think Lloyds is a competition for us in the -- their competition -- a little competition for us at the Raipur area.

guidance.t: So actual capex would be -- we expect around INR4,000 crores this year.

Guidance & outlook: We have locked in approximately 3,112 crores of CAPEX this year which is already we have exceeded last year and we expect to have a CAPEX of around 4,000 crores in this financial year.

Also, we have a major vendor conference where about 150 vendors participated, more than 250 people were there where we unveiled our plan for CAPEX of around 70,000 crores for the next five to six years to enable us to reach 100 million tons target.
So, that is why if you match it to sales, it will not give about 20% that you are expecting, so because of about 50 lakh tons.
Growth & demand: And obviously we are terminating our last pipeline, we will also be setting up at least an 8 million tons pellet plant there.

This is just next to the Gangavaram port, 1,500 crores have been paid to RVNL and we are in the process of registering that land, but as of now we have already taken possession and made the boun dary wall, now we are making plans to make investments, the three investments as I said, blending yard, pellet plant and pipeline.
Because last time in 2021 there was an additional 22.5% premium we had to absorb it and only gradually depending on the demand/supply situation, we were able to occasionally pass on.
Margins & costs: The first one is, if I look at th e royalty as a percentage of realization, it's around 46% this quarter, much higher than the last two qua rters.
Once the rights issue were subscribed, I think we subscribed around 22 million and the subscribers had subscribed their cost.
So, when we look at our finance cost, that has gone up from 29 crores to 61 crores for this quarter and year-on-year the number is up from 32.
Capex & expansion: And for note #8, it's regarding our investment in RNIL to the tune of Rs.1,500 crores for setting up of various facility.
You outlined 70,000 crores CAPEX for increasing to 100 million tons whereas the current gross block on the book that you have for 50 million tons is much significant ly lower.

I expect the pellet plant will be commissioned by the end of this calendar year, but what we are executing now and completing is a 2 million tons pellet plant with the provision of upgrading into 6 million tons.
Balance sheet & cash: And also the NMDC February 10, 2025 receivables to the tune of 3,000 crores something pending from them also.
As on December 24, the receivables from RINL is to the tune of 3,400 crores.

The working capital requirements have gone up and as you know now that we are trying to get this down instead of investing into FDs, our surplus cash, we are now liquidating our working capital loan that has accrued, so that we're taking care of that.
Risks & challenges: So, we are headwinds in terms of prices, but we are trying to see what best can be done.

guidance.t: We have locked in approximately 3,112 crores of CAPEX this year which is already we have exceeded last year and we expect to have a CAPEX of around 4,000 crores in this financial year.
